core_obligations: Reduce to the fpqc case using the inclusions among the five topologies (proof lines 2386-2395).
Assume an fpqc covering and a family of sections s_i of f_i^* f^* F agreeing on the double fibre products (proof lines 2396-2400).
Reinterpret the sections as maps f_i^* O_T -> f_i^* f^* F compatible with the canonical descent data on O_T and f^* F (proof lines 2401-2404).
Apply fpqc descent for quasi-coherent modules to obtain a unique descended map O_T -> f^* F, which is the required section (proof lines 2405-2408).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the fpqc topology (proof lines 2386-2395).
Sections as compatible maps out of the structure sheaf (proof lines 2396-2404).
Descent of the map and conclusion (proof lines 2405-2408).
difficulty_reason: For a quasi-coherent module F on a scheme S and a topology tau among Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf and fpqc, the lemma asserts that the functor of (equation-quasi-coherent-presheaf) satisfies the sheaf condition for every tau-covering of every scheme T over S (statement lines 2374-2383). The proof reduces to the fpqc case by the chain of inclusions among the topologies, which are quoted from Topologies; then a family of compatible sections of f_i^* f^* F over the covering is reinterpreted as a family of maps O_{T_i} -> f_i^* f^* F compatible with the canonical descent data on O_T and f^* F, and the fpqc descent proposition for quasi-coherent modules descends these to a unique map O_T -> f^* F, which is the required section (proof lines 2385-2408). The level is H3: the reinterpretation of sections as maps out of the structure sheaf is the conceptual step, and the descent input is a genuine effectivity statement whose hypotheses are checked in the span.
